entries.description:
# Fluent UI Contributors Packages

Welcome to the documentation site for Fluent UI Contributors packages! These packages are published under the `@fluentui-contrib/` scope and provide additional functionality to enhance your Fluent UI experience.

## Available Packages

Explore the various packages available to extend your Fluent UI capabilities:

-   [**houdini-utils**](./?path=/docs/packages-houdini-utils--docs): Utilities for CSS Houdini.
    
-   [**react-chat**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-chat-chat--docs): React component for chat interfaces.
    
-   [**react-data-grid-react-window**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-data-grid-react-window--docs): DataGrid with vertical virtualization using react-window.
    
-   [**react-data-grid-react-window-grid**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-data-grid-react-window-grid--docs): DataGrid with 2D virtualization using react-window.
    
-   [**react-draggable-dialog**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-draggable-dialog--docs): Draggable dialog component.
    
-   [**react-headless-provider**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-headless-provider--docs): Provides a replacement for `FluentProvider` that does not render additional DOM elements.
    
-   [**react-interactive-tab**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-interactive-tab--docs): InteractiveTab component enables you to include interactive elements, such as buttons, within a tab.
    
-   [**react-resize-handle**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-resize-handle--docs): Component for creating resizable layouts.
    
-   [**react-shadow**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-shadow--docs): Adapter for using Fluent UI with `react-shadow`.
    
-   [**react-tree-grid**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-tree-grid--docs): TreeGrid component for hierarchical data.
    
-   [**react-virtualizer**](./?path=/docs/packages-react-virtualizer--docs): Virtualizer hooks and scroll view component for optimizing long-list renders
    

## Getting Started

To get started with any of these packages in your project:

1.  Install the desired package using `npm` or `yarn`:
    
    ```text
    npm install @fluentui-contrib/<package-name>
    ```
    
    or
    
    ```text
    yarn add @fluentui-contrib/<package-name>
    ```
2.  Import and use the components in your React application.
    
3.  Refer to the individual package documentation (Storybook links above) for detailed usage instructions and examples.
    

## Contributing

We welcome contributions to FluentUI Contrib! If you're interested in contributing, please read our [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-contrib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for instructions on how to get started.

Thank you for being a part of the Fluent UI community!

# @fluentui-contrib/azure-theme

Azure Theme package powered by Fluent UI and used in Microsoft Azure.

# @fluentui-contrib/houdini-utils

This library exposes some low level utilities to use the [houdini APIs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Houdini_APIs)
as well as a canvas fallback that should be usable with the [paint worklet](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSS_Painting_API#the_paint_worklet) that would normally be used by houdini.

Please refer to the [documentation samples](https://microsoft.github.io/fluentui-contrib/houdini-utils/) for usage guidance

# @fluentui-contrib/react-data-grid-react-window

A variant of the Fluent UI [DataGrid](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/components-datagrid--default) that is
virtualized using [react-window](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size).

props.name: size
props.description: Affects the sizes of all table subcomponents

props.name: noNativeElements
props.description: Render all table elements as divs instead of semantic table elements Using divs no longer uses `display: table` layout but `display: flex`

props.name: sortable
props.description: Whether the table is sortable

props.name: focusMode
props.description: How focus navigation will work in the datagrid

props.name: subtleSelection
props.description: Enables subtle selection style

props.name: selectionAppearance
props.description: Row appearance when selected

props.name: resizableColumns
props.description: Enables column resizing

props.name: defaultSelectedItems
props.description: Used in uncontrolled mode to set initial selected items on mount

props.name: selectedItems
props.description: Used to control selected items

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.type: (e: MouseEvent<Element, MouseEvent> | KeyboardEvent<Element>, data: OnSelectionChangeData) => void

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: Enables row selection and sets the selection mode

props.name: columnSizingOptions
props.description: Options for column resizing, specific for each column

props.name: onColumnResize
props.type: (e: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent | TouchEvent, data: { columnId: TableColumnId; width: number; }) => void
props.description: A callback triggered when a column is resized.

props.name: containerWidthOffset
props.description: For column resizing. Allows for a container size to be adjusted by a number of pixels, to make sure the columns don't overflow the table. By default, this value is calculated internally based on other props, but can be overriden.

props.name: resizableColumnsOptions
props.description: Custom options for column resizing.

stories.name: VirtualizedDataGrid
stories.description:
Virtualizating the DataGrid component involves recomposing components to use a virtualized container.
This is already done in the extension package `@fluentui/react-data-grid-react-window` which provides
extended DataGrid components that are powered
by [react-window](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size).

The example below shows how to use this extension package to virtualize the DataGrid component.

> ⚠️ Make sure to memoize the row render function to avoid excessive unmouting/mounting of components.
react-window will [create components based on this renderer](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/api/FixedSizeList)

stories.name: ReactWindowOverrides
stories.description:
As VirtualizedDataGrid relies on [FixedListSIze](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size),
you may want to pass some props directly to it. One use case could be to add additional styling to the list itself
In this example we make sure to keep header aligned with row content no matter if list scrollbar is visible or not.
Resize window vertically to see this in action.

stories.name: DataGridScrollingIndicators
stories.description:
As VirtualizedDataGrid relies on [FixedSizeList](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size),
you may want to pass some props directly to it. If your component's items are expensive to render,
you can boost performance by rendering a placeholder while the user is scrolling.
To do this, add the `useIsScrolling` property to your List or Grid.
Now an additional parameter, `isScrolling`, will be passed to your render method.
In this example, we render a shimmer effect while the user is scrolling.

stories.name: ResizableDataGrid
stories.description:
Virtualizating the DataGrid component involves recomposing components to use a virtualized container.
This is already done in the extension package `@fluentui/react-data-grid-react-window` which provides
extended DataGrid components that are powered
by [react-window](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/examples/list/fixed-size).

The example below shows how to use this extension package to virtualize the DataGrid component.

> ⚠️ Make sure to memoize the row render function to avoid excessive unmouting/mounting of components.
react-window will [create components based on this renderer](https://react-window.vercel.app/#/api/FixedSizeList)

# @fluentui-contrib/react-draggable-dialog

A draggable dialog component powered by Fluent UI.

props.name: surfaceMotion
props.description: For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

props.name: modalType
props.description: Dialog variations.  `modal`: When this type of dialog is open, the rest of the page is dimmed out and cannot be interacted with. The tab sequence is kept within the dialog and moving the focus outside the dialog will imply closing it. This is the default type of the component.  `non-modal`: When a non-modal dialog is open, the rest of the page is not dimmed out and users can interact with the rest of the page. This also implies that the tab focus can move outside the dialog when it reaches the last focusable element.  `alert`: is a special type of modal dialogs that interrupts the user's workflow to communicate an important message or ask for a decision. Unlike a typical modal dialog, the user must take an action through the options given to dismiss the dialog, and it cannot be dismissed through the dimmed background.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls the open state of the dialog

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Default value for the uncontrolled open state of the dialog.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the component changes value from open state. @param event - a React's Synthetic event or a KeyboardEvent in case of `documentEscapeKeyDown` @param data - A data object with relevant information, such as open value and type of interaction that created the event

props.name: inertTrapFocus
props.description: Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal) where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.

props.name: id
props.description: Unique identifier for the draggable dialog.

props.name: boundary
props.description: Element to be used as a boundary when dragging the dialog.

props.name: margin
props.description: The margin from the boundary to keep the element in when dragged. Only used when boundary is set.

props.name: position
props.description: Initial position of the dialog. - Only works when boundary is set. - If not set, the dialog will be centered within the boundary. - If set, the dialog will be positioned at the specified coordinates, relative to the boundary.

props.name: onPositionChange
props.description: Event triggered when the dialog is dragged.

props.name: announcements
props.description: Text to be announced by screen readers when the dialog is dragged.

# @fluentui-contrib/react-gamepad-navigation

**Gamepad Navigation for [Fluent UI React](https://react.fluentui.dev/)**

> [!WARNING]
> These are not production-ready components and **should never be used in product**. This space is useful for testing new components whose APIs might change before final release.

This package provides gamepad navigation support for Fluent UI Components.
Any gaming controller implementing the [Gamepad API](https://w3c.github.io/gamepad/) is supported. Major brand controllers such as Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, 8bit, etc. are supported.

This hook calls [useArrowNavigationGroup](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/utilities-focus-management-usearrownavigationgroup--docs) and [useFocusableGroup](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/utilities-focus-management-usefocusablegroup--docs) internally.
For that reason, 'useGamepadNavigationGroup' hook uses the same API and configuration as those two previous hooks.

In addition to gamepad navigation, arrow key navigation is available by calling this hook, so there is no need to call `useArrowNavigationGroup` separately.

# @fluentui/react-headless-provider

A package that provides a headless provider, a replacement in some cases for `FluentProvider` from `@fluentui/react-components`.

`HeadlessFluentProvider` does not render additional any DOM elements, only applies React Contexts needed for components from `@fluentui/react-components` to render properly.

Following features work:

- rendering into different documents i.e. `targetDocument` prop
- `customStyleHooks_unstable` & `overrides_unstable` props

Following features don't work:

- scoped theming, in this scenario theming should be configured globally or separately
- scoped "dir", in this scenario text direction should be configured globally or separately
- polyfill for `:focus-visible` (`useFocusVisible()` from `@fluentui/react-tabster`) should be initialized separately

Designed to be used with [`createCSSRuleFromTheme()`](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/pull/29052), see for context [microsoft/fluentui#21290](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/issues/21290).

stories.name: Default
stories.description: This example uses iframe to sandbox styles, but it's not mandatory in a real world. This example uses HeadlessFluentProvider to provide proper context values for components (including a proper document instance), but does not apply CSS for the theme. CSS for theme is applied globally (to `:root`) in this example.

# @fluentui-contrib/react-interactive-tab

The `InteractiveTab` component is an extension of the Tab component from `@fluentui/react-components`. It allows you to add interactive elements, such as buttons, inside a tab.

props.description: Root of the component.

props.name: content
props.description: Component children are placed in this slot Avoid using the `children` property in this slot in favour of Component children whenever possible.

props.name: button
props.description: The button that represents the tab. This is the element that will be focused when the tab is selected.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon that renders before the content.

props.name: contentBefore
props.description: Element before the button, within the tab

props.name: contentAfter
props.description: Element after the button, within the tab

entries.description: # @fluentui-contrib/react-keytips

stories.name: Default
stories.description:
By default Keytips are shown for all target elements that have keytip attached via
`useKeytipRef`, except disabled elements.
When multiple Keytips start with the same character, typing that character will filter the visible keytips.
You can also use `positioning` to set an offset from the target element, or control [other positioning options](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/concepts-developer-positioning-components--docs).

stories.name: WithTabs
stories.description: For Tabs, Keytips will first show keytip for each tab, after selecting a tab, the keytips foor it's content are shown.

stories.name: Dynamic
stories.description:
If a `Keytip` triggers dynamic content that includes its own keytips, you must add the `dynamic` prop to the `useKeytipRef` for the relevant component. Additionally, the child keytips should include the parents key sequence in their key sequences.

Take the case below; clicking Button 1 and Button 2 will update the text of Button3. Triggering the keytip for Button 1 or Button 2 will then also change the keytip sequence of Button 3, because it can be both a child of Button 1 or Button 2. For this to work fully, Button 1 and Button 2 should have `dynamic: true`.

stories.name: Shortcut
stories.description:
Keytips with `Overflow` and `Menu` components offer special options:

`hasMenu` - Indicates that the Keytip opens a submenu. If hasMenu is not provided, the Keytip will trigger `onExecute` directly instead of displaying a submenu.

In this example, firing `T`, `Y` and `R` will show this functionality.

# @fluentui-contrib/react-resize-handle

This library adds support for mouse and keyboard resizing of components/panels in your UI. It has proper a11y, works well with flex and grid layouts and is flexible enough to not require any drastic changes in your layout.

Use your mouse or touch to drag the element, or focus it and use the arrow keys to resize (step is 20px).

It also works with HTML elements directly without going through the React lifecycle. This and the fact that it relies on the CSS layouting engine makes sure it is very performant.

![Demo](public/demo.gif 'Demo')

# @fluentui-contrib/react-shadow

This package provides a React component that renders its children inside a shadow DOM.

stories.name: InsertionPoint
stories.description:
The insertion order of Fluent styles can be controlled with a sentinal "insertion point" stylesheet.
              This is useful for controlling specificity when using styles outside of Fluent.

# @fluentui-contrib/react-themeless-provider

This package provides `ThemelessFluentProvider`, a replacement for `FluentProvider` when the provider needs to be rendered inside shadow DOM.

`ThemelessFluentProvider` does not render the theme contexts or inject theme CSS custom properties into the DOM. When using this provider you are responsible for setting the necessary CSS custom properties in such a way that they will pierce the shadow DOM (e.g., apply them to `:root`).

props.name: dir
props.description: Sets the direction of text & generated styles.

props.name: customStyleHooks_unstable
props.type: Partial<{ useAccordionHeaderStyles_unstable: CustomStyleHook; useAccordionItemStyles_unstable: CustomStyleHook; useAccordionPanelStyles_unstable: CustomStyleHook; ... 189 more ...; useVirtualizerStyles_unstable: CustomStyleHook; }>
props.description: Sets the hooks for custom styling components.

props.name: targetDocument
props.description: Provides the document, can be undefined during SSR render.

# react-virtualizer

This library was generated with [Nx](https://nx.dev).

<!-- Don't allow prettier to collapse code block into single line -->
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
>
> ```jsx
>
> import { VirtualizerScrollView } from '@fluentui-contrib/react-virtualizer';
>
> ```
>
> - Features and APIs may change before final release
> - Please contact us if you intend to use this in your product
>
> VirtualizerScrollView provides an out of the box static (uniform row/column sizing) implementation of Virtualizer hooks
>
> If looking for dynamic sizes or auto-measuring features, use VirtualizerScrollViewDynamic

<!-- Don't allow prettier to collapse code block into single line -->
<!-- prettier-ignore -->
>
> ```jsx
>
> import { VirtualizerScrollViewDynamic } from '@fluentui-contrib/react-virtualizer';
>
> ```
>
> - Features and APIs may change before final release
> - Please contact us if you intend to use this in your product
>
> VirtualizerScrollViewDynamic provides an out of the box virtualizer implementation for dynamic or variant sized columns/rows
>
> This component has auto enabled measuring functionality when getItemSize is not passed in as prop function.
>
> If rows/columns are known uniform sizes, use VirtualizerScrollView instead
